sent_bad: 1. The 16-year-old likely can't be your care provider.
Since the 16-year-old is your husband's daughter (under 19) and, if she is a dependent you or your spouse may claim on your return, she would be disqualified as a care provider.
2. The 16-year-old is not a qualifying individual.

Your 11-year-old daughter *is* a qualifying individual (a dependent child under 13), so if you paid an *eligible* care provider (not a dependent you can claim, not a child under 19, etc.) for her care while you worked or actively looked for work, you could claim the credit — up to $3,000 for one qualifying individual (or $6,000 for two or more), subject to the earned-income limit and the percentag
So, paying your husband's 16-year-old daughter to babysit would not qualify you for the credit under the rules in this document.
